findings.title: Legacy QR preview documentation still describes a diagnostic decision as signing approval

No current signing authority follows from those booleans.

security_analysis.conclusion: One fixed-schema Reader replaces both permissive scanners. Decoded names are compared before dispatch, so aliases cannot bypass uniqueness or the allowlist. Complete-object consumption, exact decimal unsigned lexemes, u16 kind, interoperable timestamp policy, strict UTF-8/surrogates, tag shape and aggregate capacities fail closed. Unknown fields reject without recursively traversing their values. EventTemplate owns decoded values once and canonicalizes order-preserving NIP-01 strings/arrays with the exact accepted seven escapes plus lowercase other-C0 escapes. Standalone write_canonical accepts public bytes for a diagnostic calculation; authorization never takes that caller output as identity or authority.

A non-Clone owner consumes the S02 secret, derives its actual x-only identity and retains one immutable parsed request. The private pending context binds request, account/session/policy/operation/configuration, exact review, limits, geometry and deadline. start_execution changes Approved to Spent before correlation/time/binding validation or backend invocation. Completion is revalidated, verifies raw BIP340 against the bound key/ID, invalidates unconditionally, and has no response cache. Execution borrows the original owner exclusively; safe external callers cannot detach or retarget it to a reconstructed owner with repeated numeric counters. Existing authored fault-injection and race tests were inspected and independently rerun; public lifecycle probes add rejected configuration and same-key account replacement controls.

Cancel, lock/reset, policy/account/configuration changes and unavailable/rolled-back/expired time clear pending authority. Busy intake cannot replace the request or extend deadline. Full traversal has no jumping API; every successful local Next advances one flat page and a distinct final decision is required. Failed display cannot acknowledge; early approval or duplicate consent is terminal. LocalReviewIo and supplied monotonic ticks are trusted-image adapter responsibilities: malicious firmware can lie, so this is not a sandbox or physical button attestation. Future transport connection teardown/rebind must invoke invalidation on this same owner; current legacy transports are signing-disabled and do not create owner authority. There is no qualified asynchronous provider or live reconnect integration in S03.

Only the accepted kind-1 subset reaches this owner. Known e/p/q prefixes validate curve keys, markers/reply context, quote address structure and conservative URI grammar; invalid known semantics and emoji never fall back to uninterpreted acceptance. Unknown tags and defined suffixes are complete indexed additional signed data. Every signed field, identity, correlation and bound local context is paginated with label/value/position accounting. Quoting plus escaped literal backslash makes the ASCII token grammar injective, including literal escape text versus bidi/combining/control/supplementary scalars. Tokens never split across lines in the independent reconstruction. This proves exact inspection, not readable Unicode UX, high-level reply education or actual screen/input usability.

Single 4096-byte decoded arena, bounded spans/tag boundaries and one pending slot avoid the former Cartesian allocation risk. Host retained EventTemplate/Pending/AuthorizationSession sizes independently reproduced as 5232/5728/6016 bytes, within 8192/16384 caps also compiled for RISC-V. Canonical hash streams; no canonical copy, page array, queue or completed-result cache lives in the owner. The narrow parser/semantic-review/owner modules remain understandable without a generic authorization registry. Frame lookup recomputes the bounded document and a full review can be quadratic in page count; actual peak stack/RAM and latency remain explicit device gates. This source review does not infer those measurements from fixed type sizes.

security_analysis.area: Shipping boundary, dependencies and key material
security_analysis.conclusion: Product attempt_sign supplies only SigningUnavailable to the private consuming boundary; the actual sign_raw call is in a private cfg(test) module, with no public secret callback, mint, test feature or production enable switch. No obsolete can_sign/approved_for_signing authority API remains; the historical fixture field reader is diagnostic. The activated no-default runtime graph includes k256 Schnorr/arithmetic and transitive ecdsa DER/digest support, but no alloc/std/serde/ECDH/getrandom or ECDSA algorithm feature. rand_core traits do not create an entropy provider. All lock package checksums and 1869 vendor file hashes match; provenance/license source is retained. S02 intake wipes caller storage; k256 Drop zeroizes its retained scalar, but conversion copies/moves, scalar temporaries, compiler spills and backend scratch are not proven erased. k256 normalizes d to n-d for even Y and keeps only that scalar; future recovery custody must preserve the original imported source before conversion. No recovery export or NIP44 path is implemented; scalar negation alone is not evidence of an NIP44 x-coordinate failure.
